entry.title: Trim redundant Actions triggers and stop the failing Dependabot retri…
entry.content:
Trim redundant Actions triggers and stop the failing Dependabot retries (#10)

Each merged PR was fanning out to roughly six workflow runs, and a few of
them had nothing to do.

- CodeQL had no concurrency group, so pushing repeatedly to a PR left
  superseded analyses running to completion alongside the current one. CI
  already cancelled these; CodeQL now does too, on PRs only, since a main
  run establishes the default-branch alert baseline.

- CodeQL now skips paths that contain no first-party JS/TS. That covers
  docs- and asset-only changes, and incidentally all of Dependabot: each
  ecosystem touches exactly one ignored path. CodeQL is not a required
  check, so a filtered-out run cannot block a merge.

- The CI safety-net rebuild ran nightly to cover auto-merges that never
  fire the push trigger, but those only arrive with Dependabot's Monday
  batch. Six of the seven weekly runs rebuilt an unchanged main.

- The auto-merge workflow re-ran on every `synchronize`, though enabling
  auto-merge sticks for the life of the PR.

- Dependabot's `cookie` and `esbuild` security updates are transitive-only
  and unreachable from any direct bump, so they failed on every run. Both
  are now ignored, with the reasoning recorded; the alerts stay visible in
  the Security tab.

Required checks are untouched — CI keeps running on every push and PR.

Co-authored-by: Chenophobia <yao.chen@streambow.com>
Co-authored-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

entry.title: Consistent curriculum naming scheme and an app icon (#9)
entry.content:
Consistent curriculum naming scheme and an app icon (#9)

* docs: design spec for curriculum naming scheme and app icon

* feat: consistent curriculum naming scheme and an app icon

Unit titles had drifted across three authoring passes into four competing
conventions: positional numbering that repeated its own chapter ("Kanji
Set 1 — Core & most useful"), colons in vocabulary against em dashes in
grammar, bare grammar titles alongside "Topic — gloss" ones, one raw
Japanese title, and "&"/"and" used interchangeably. The Hiragana and
Katakana chapters named the same material differently on three of five
units.

Settle on one scheme and rename 23 of 50 units to match. naming.test.ts
enforces the rules mechanically, which is what stops the next authoring
pass from inventing a fifth convention — an explicit list of expected
titles catches a title changing, not a new title arriving wrong.

Titles now sync in place on startup instead of via `reseed`. Renaming
changes no card content, so it has no business dropping and re-inserting
`cards` and taking every user's FSRS state, streaks, and review history
with it. syncCurriculumTitles matches rows by position and writes only
`title`, and verifies the database's shape matches the curriculum's
first — position stops identifying the same unit the moment a unit is
added or reordered, and renaming by position would then silently retitle
the wrong rows. That case warns and writes nothing; `reseed` stays the
escape hatch.

Replace SvelteKit's default Svelte-logo favicon with a white あ on the
app's indigo accent, as PNGs for the browser tab and the iPad homescreen.
The glyph is rendered from the system font at build time by
scripts/make-icons.sh: an SVG <text> element would render as tofu on any
device without a Japanese font.

The icon <link href>s are root-absolute rather than %sveltekit.assets%,
which expands to a relative "." and so resolved to
/study/apple-touch-icon.png — a 404 — on every nested route. iOS reads
the touch icon from whichever page is open when you add to the
homescreen, so that silently degraded the shortcut to a screenshot. The
old favicon.svg had the same flaw.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Chenophobia <yao.chen@streambow.com>
Co-authored-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

entry.title: Dependency-PR grouping, action bumps, and public-docs sanitization (#7)
entry.content:
Dependency-PR grouping, action bumps, and public-docs sanitization (#7)

* ci: group Dependabot majors and ignore bumps that can never apply

The first Dependabot run opened three separate PRs, two of which could
never be merged: TypeScript 7 fails `npm ci` outright (SvelteKit declares
`peerOptional typescript "^5.3.3 || ^6.0.0"`), and node:25 is an
odd-numbered line that never becomes LTS and went EOL on 2026-03-31 —
CI passes it happily because building an image says nothing about whether
the base is still supported.

Both are now ignored at the major level, and majors that do matter arrive
as one grouped PR per ecosystem instead of one per package. Everything is
scheduled at the same hour so a week's updates land together.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* ci: take the grouped GitHub Actions major bumps

Supersedes Dependabot's own PR for these, with one change: it pinned
CodeQL to the patch tag v4.37.3, which would generate a PR for every
CodeQL patch release. The floating v4 major tag is used instead, matching
every other action here.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs: remove tunnel ids and host paths from the public docs

This repo is public. The deployment docs carried the Cloudflare Tunnel's
id (twice, including in a copy-pasteable `tunnel route dns` command), the
credentials-file path, the ingress map for an unrelated site sharing the
tunnel, and the operator's home directory. None of it is a credential —
the tunnel secret lives in ~/.cloudflared and was never committed — but
all of it is free reconnaissance and none of it helps a reader.

The architecture and the reasoning behind it are unchanged; only the
identifiers are now placeholders. The launchd plist becomes a template
with __REPO__ substituted at install time, since launchd needs an
absolute path but the repo does not need to name anyone's home directory.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: keep the deploy log quiet unless something actually happened

Installing the launchd agent showed that `docker compose` narrates
"Pulling / Pulled / Running" on stderr even with --quiet-pull. At one poll
every 5 minutes that is ~860 lines a day, so the log this script writes
would have been pure noise with the occasional real deploy buried in it.

Each step's output is now captured and replayed only on failure: a healthy
poll writes nothing, a broken one writes a timestamped failure and the
command's output, and the script still exits non-zero so launchd records it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Chenophobia <yao.chen@streambow.com>
Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entry.title: Tests, CI/CD pipeline, and code-quality gates (#3)
entry.content:
Tests, CI/CD pipeline, and code-quality gates (#3)

* test: cover the auth guard, route actions, and small lib helpers

37 new tests: hooks.server.ts (login redirects with next preservation,
stale-cookie cleanup, theme handling), the study rate action (400/409/ok
paths) and load's three empty-queue shapes, the login action (bad
credentials, session cookie, remember-me, safe next), logout, the theme
API, parseCardFaces, and utcDayStart boundary arithmetic.

Route modules read the db singleton at import time, so these tests swap
it for an in-memory database via vi.mock and drive the real handlers.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* style: add prettier + eslint as the lint gate, format the repo

eslint flat config: js/ts/svelte recommended sets, prettier compat.
no-navigation-without-resolve is off (no paths.base); the two deliberate
patterns it flagged (control-char regex in safe-redirect, bare
dependency read in ThemeToggle's effect) carry inline disables with
rationale. Real finds fixed: keyed the nav {#each}. One-time
prettier --write over the repo (mostly tailwind class ordering).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* ci: GitHub Actions pipeline, Dependabot auto-merge, pull-based deploy

CI: lint + svelte-check + vitest + build on every push/PR; green main
builds the linux/arm64 image (native arm runner) and pushes it to GHCR.
CodeQL on push/PR/weekly. Dependabot watches npm (minor/patch grouped),
actions, and the Dockerfile base image; its minor/patch PRs auto-merge
only after CI passes, majors wait for review.

Deploy is pull-based (public repo, so no self-hosted runner): a launchd
agent on the host runs deploy/update.sh every 5 minutes, restarting the
container only when GHCR has a new image. Nightly CI rebuild covers the
GITHUB_TOKEN quirk where auto-merged pushes don't trigger workflows.

entry.title: refactor: dedupe Card.svelte's face classes into one shared constant
entry.content:
refactor: dedupe Card.svelte's face classes into one shared constant

The two card faces are stacked in a single grid cell and must stay
dimensionally identical, or the card changes size mid-flip. Repeating ~10
utility classes on each face risked a one-sided edit breaking that
invariant silently. Extract them into a single `face` constant used by
both, keeping only the genuinely per-face bits (the rotateY transform,
inert/aria-hidden) inline.

entry.title: fix: always clear rating in-flight flag, even on a rejected update()
entry.content:
fix: always clear rating in-flight flag, even on a rejected update()

use:enhance's update() (and the explicit invalidateAll() after it) can
reject on a network failure. Without a finally, that left submitting and
rating.inFlight stuck true forever, which silently disabled cross-device
revalidation for the rest of the page's life — on exactly the flaky mobile
connectivity this feature exists to handle. Wrap the body in try/finally so
both flags always reset regardless of outcome.

entry.title: fix: mirror revealed answer onto shared revalidation flag
entry.content:
fix: mirror revealed answer onto shared revalidation flag

The study page is the only place that knows whether the current card's
answer is showing and unrated. Mirror `revealed` onto the shared
rating.answerRevealed flag (added in the previous commit) so the layout's
revalidation listeners can see it, and clear it on teardown so a stale
`true` can't outlive navigation away from /study.

entry.title: fix: suppress revalidation while a card's answer is revealed
entry.content:
fix: suppress revalidation while a card's answer is revealed

invalidateAll() on visibility restore was replacing `data` unconditionally,
and the study page's reveal-reset effect keys off `data` itself (not the
card id) so it could not tell a genuine new card from a refetch of the same
one. Every tab-switch/app-switcher/notification-pulldown on iPad flipped a
revealed answer back to the question.

Add a shared `rating.answerRevealed` flag, mirrored from the study page's
local `revealed` state, and have shouldRevalidate() skip revalidation
whenever it's set: the server would just serve back the same card, so
refetching only destroys reading position for no benefit. Covered with
mutation-checked tests in revalidate.test.ts.
